title: Composables: reusable behavior without hidden global state
outcome: Extract reactive behavior with explicit inputs, lifecycle cleanup, and a predictable return API.
useCase: Selection, pagination, subscriptions, and reusable editor behavior.
drawbacks: Hidden singleton state and implicit dependencies can make bugs travel.
version: Modern JavaScript / TypeScript · Vue 3.5 where applicable · browser APIs
cue: Inputs visible. State owned. Effects cleaned up.

trace.title: Explicit input
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

A composable is a function that packages reusable stateful logic. It is not simply any helper with use in its name.

A pure formatter is often just a function.

Choose where state is created. A ref inside useSelection gives each call its own selection.

A ref at module scope is shared by every caller in that JavaScript runtime. That can be deliberate for a store, but dangerous for per-request state in server rendering.

Return refs when callers need to destructure reactive values. Accept a getter/ref when the input should remain live, and watch that input explicitly.

Register lifecycle cleanup while the component context is available. Detached listeners, intervals, and subscriptions must have a lifetime owner.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Two components call useSelection. Each call allocates one ref, so they can select different tickets.

Move the ref above the function and both callers now share it. Neither version is automatically better; the intended ownership decides.

Test composables with pure seams when possible. For lifecycle-dependent behavior, mount a small component and verify listeners are removed when it unmounts.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: Creating a timer without clearing it can keep updating a vanished view. A composable that silently reads route, store, and global user state is harder to reuse than one with explicit dependencies.
